notes.title: Build 0.5.20 - Auto Adventures, Rest System, Skill Improvements!
notes.content:
This patch brings quite a few changes so please read through carefully so that a lot frustrations can be avoided.

[b]!!!IMPORTANT!!!
- You MUST abandon all Adventures upon loading in the game with this new patch.
- You MUST reset all skills for all Adventurers or skills will be broken for those Adventurers.[/b]

[b]Skills[/b]
- All Class Skill trees have been improved.
- Skills now unlock at levels 1, 5 and 10.
- You may only spec in maximum of 5 Skills. Passives are not included in this count.
- All Skills now have 10 Ranks instead of 5.
- Stuns are no longer a guaranteed success, they improve with more Ranks. They are no longer 'one-point wonders,' sorry!
- Investing Skill Points into a skill has increasing costs at Ranks 5 and 9.  What this means is Ranks 1-4 costs 1 Point, 5-8 costs 2 Points, and 9-10 costs 3 points.

[b]Gameplay[/b]
- The Adventurers menu has been reworked.
- Automatic Adventures are now taken from a master list of available Adventures located on the main map UI screen.
- Auto Adventures no longer "turn in."  Instead they tick every 2 minutes and grant XP and gold closely resembling a manual encounter.
- Adventurers may now be hired at levels 1, 10, 20 and 30 depending on the Allegiance level of the town they are being hired in. They also have associated gold costs.
- 2Handed Weapons now roll double stats to make them more useful.

[b]Resting System[/b]
- Adventurers now have a new stat called Endurance which slowly drains as they defeat encounters in dungeons and run Automatic Adventures.
- When an Adventurer reaches 0 endurance in an Auto Adventure the Adventure will automatically end.
- Resting Adventurers at the Inns located in each town will help them regain Endurance.
- Starting at 30 endurance Adventurers will become fatigued and take a big hit to their stats.  The rate of decay is exponential as the Adventurer's endurance goes to 0.

[b]Art[/b]
- Race icons were added to several screens.
- All skill icons have been added to the game.
- The Inn scene has been added to the game!
- Hiring Adventurers menu has been moved to the lonely Warrior standing outside the Inn.
- An all new party creation screen has been introduced.

[b]Other[/b]
- Slightly reduced the time to wait between an encounter ending and proceeding to the next room.
- Lots of other minor tweaks and bug fixes.

notes.title: Devlog #7
notes.content:
[i]Hello!

Welcome to the 7th edition of AM Devlog! AM Devlogs are weekly updates (when we don't patch) on the development progress of Adventurer Manager. These Devlogs highlight our philosophy of the importance of development transparency and player feedback.

Missed a Devlog? You can view the archive [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/280320/discussions/0/540740501567633716/]here![/url][/i]

I want to start off this 7th Devlog talking about some upcoming Skill adjustments. While the previously introduced 'major' patch adjusted Skill drastically we knew that it wouldn't be a simple one and done. We've introduced a few hotfixes along the way to address some overpowered classes and abilities. This upcoming patch will introduce even more changes to the the way Skills work and we think we are very close to a final iteration! Here's the details of the new system. We've reduced the total amount of Skills down from 12 Active, 4 Passive to 9 Active, 3 Passive. Wait, what?! You took away Skills?! Yes we did! While we were happy with the amount of Skill options available to you all, we did not like the amount of redundancies that were occurring within the same class. Fewer Skills allows us to really make those Skills more vital. In addition, you will now have to CHOOSE 5 of those 9 Active Skills to specialize in. Once you choose your 5 you are locked into those selections until you pay lots of gold to respec them. In order to make your 5 choices more important, the total investable Skill ranks for them will increase to 10 and they will matter. 'One point wonders' will largely be removed due to the fact that the first Skill Point into a Skill will not ultimately be worth it, but over 5-10 Ranks you will see definite gains. One of the most important elements that have been changed regarding the Skills are Stuns. Stuns are no longer 100% guaranteed. Stuns will now have a % chance to land and will increase with invested Ranks. All of these changes are getting us closer to our goal of making Adventurer Manager's combat more tactical and engaging.

WARNING! Monsters are going to get a helluva lot tougher in the very near future. You all have had it relatively easy but it was never the intention for you to breeze through our dungeon content! You will soon see the introduction of various Monster mutators that will influence their strengths and weaknesses! Enraged and Deadly Monsters will go away and instead Enraged and Deadly will be two of many possible mutators that a pack of Monsters in any dungeon can contain. An example of some mutators include: Deadly, increased Critical Hit Chance; Shielding, increased Block Chance; Armored, increased Armor; Tough, increased HP; and so forth. These mutators will also apply to minibosses and bosses and will undoubtedly make them much tougher to take down. To help you identify what a particular monster or group of monster has a Mutator, there will be new info pane that will appear to give you more detailed information.

The goal for combat and dungeon exploring in AM is to have our basic encounters be relatively easy to allow you to farm and gather equipment to prepare you for the tougher encounters which require careful utilization of classes, abilities, and equipment to take down. You may encounter a boss with high block chance and realize a Paladin would be very helpful to debuff the block chance. That's not to say it will be impossible without a Paladin, merely you may find some combinations of Classes more useful for certain situations. I'm happy to say that gone will be the days where you can AoE breeze your way through our dungeons!

The vision for AM has always been the management of your Adventurers and part of that will be how/when to utilize certain classes and equipment over others depending on the Monster and Dungeon and next patch should be a step in that direction. I apologize in advance for any trouble these new monsters may cause, (just kidding, I want to kill all of your Adventurers as much as possible *evil grin*) but it should be a lot more challenging which is what we've always wanted in AM!

Skills will not be complete with these changes though! Pretty soon you will see the introduction of the aforementioned Class and Power Party abilities. Your favorite AoE stuns and heals (and even resurrect) will be introduced! Just to recap: Power will generate after multiple encounters of using Skills, taking damage, and defending to allow you to utilize a Class or Party 'ultimate' that you select beforehand. There will be 3-4 options per Class that will be a permanent selection. Do you want your Cleric to AoE Stun, AoE Heal, or Resurrect? These are the types of choices you'll make with your Class Power Skill. Oh and you might expect some Bosses to use some of these against you as well….

[url=http://steamcommunity.com/gid/103582791435442202/announcements/detail/1838906349694065217]Last Devlog[/url] I mentioned briefly the changes that are coming to how Auto Adventures are taken and completed and I'd like to elaborate in this weeks Devlog. Pretty soon you will see a large Scroll UI (mentioned in [url=http://steamcommunity.com/gid/103582791435442202/announcements/detail/1856918122073362772]Devlog #3[/url]) that will be your one-stop shop for Auto Adventure management. Auto Adventures will ONLY be taken from this UI. You will simply choose the level of the Adventure and the Party you would like to send and voila, they will begin the Adventure. Automatic Adventures will also take a lot longer to complete than before, but the Adventurers will steadily gain levels and Equipment as they continue along. They will end up gaining similar amounts of XP, Gold, and Equipment as if you sent them on a bunch of Auto Adventures. We'd like to cut down on the amount of micromanaging you have to do and we believe this is a step in the right direction. When the Adventure is complete, you will be notified and you simply click and Complete in the Scroll UI. You can then either Rest them or send them on another Adventure immediately! This should allow you to quickly build up secondary parties with very little hassle and clicking!

That's all for this week's edition of AM Devlog! Check back next week for more development updates and a new team member feature!

[i]Happy Adventuring![/i]
Thomas Spradling
Game Designer & Producer
VAStudios

notes.content:
[i]Hello!

Welcome to the 6th edition of AM Devlog! AM Devlogs are weekly updates (when we don't patch) on the development progress of Adventurer Manager. These Devlogs highlight our philosophy of the importance of development transparency and player feedback.

Missed a Devlog? You can view the archive [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/280320/discussions/0/540740501567633716/]here![/url][/i]

The Skill Update finally arrived last weekend! We've been wanting these skill changes for a while and are incredibly excited that you're finally getting to play it! We have already released a few hotfixes to fix and balance some abilities for various classes and we will continue to do so up to and after the full release. Skill icons are also sneaking into the game and you should see all of them fully implemented sometime next week. Player skill effects are also being slowly introduced.

One thing that we have mentioned in some discussion posts but have not officially addressed related to the Skills Update are the upcoming changes to monster skills. Over the course of some smaller patches, monsters will start receiving specific skills relevant to their type as well as overall improvements. Normal monsters will generally have one to three skills that are from their respective class but with different names and animations. This way you will know what types of abilities they use but their names and animations will differ. Animations for monster skills will definitely be introduced as we finalize them. Bosses and minibosses will have selected skills based on their classes as well but will generally be modified to make them tougher and may have some unique abilities to make things more interesting. They will also be more intelligent as to when they are using their abilities instead of blowing their best skill right at the start. It will take us a while to plug away at monster skills so we appreciate your patience as we continue to work on them.

A new system will be also introduced in the towns to hire Adventurers. Around the time the Resting system hits we will replace the Hire Adventurer menu in the Inn with a new scene for Resting Adventurers. Adventurers will now be depicted as little characters in the blank area in the bottom right below the inn. Each class will have its own unique image and animation and you'll simply click the class of Adventurer you'd like to hire and a new popup will appear. This new popup menu will show the race, class, gender, and their Attributes. As always, UI changes and improvements are always ongoing!

[img=https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog6/adv_hire_ui_preview.png]
[i]Early Hire Preview[/i]

Speaking of the Resting system, which was addressed in [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/280320/announcements/detail/1856916387695676609]Devlog #1[/url], it has received some updates that we are excited about! notes.title: Build 0.5.07 Hotfix + Changes
notes.content:
Some key changes to the game have been made that will greatly alter how combat is approached.  It was never the intention for all fights to be 1 round stun lock wipes. As we begin to implement more skills for monsters they will eventually lay down the law on Adventurers just as hard as players are to them right now.

With that said, we have normalized damage output across classes to be much closer while still maintaining obvious differences.  Aside from that... stop one shotting the poor bosses on heroic please. ;)

Here's some of the major changes that have gone in:

- The monsters in the cave have had their toughness reduced to help new ease players into the game and get some gear.
- AOE stuns have been [b]removed[/b] from the game and skills with stuns have had their damage decreased slightly.
- Surprise attacks now reduce the Energy of the party instead of stunning every party member for one round.
- Monsters have become better at finding better equpment.
- A major pass was performed for skills and the damage/healing output of classes. Skill damage was normalized to not allow for such powerful tier 4 abilities but still retain their burst nature. Fights should actually last a few rounds now and be more engaging and tactical than before.

notes.title: Build 0.5.00 Combat Overhaul
notes.content:
Hello loyal early adopters :)  This week we are bringing you part 1 of a series of combat overhauls.  This patch introduces all 8 classes to the game and sn entirely new skill system.  Expect balance passes to occur periodically as EA continues.

[b]As promised there will be a required wipe for this build.[/b]

[b]Combat 2.0[/b]
- All Adventurers now start with a basic attack and 1 skill point to train into a tier one skill.
- Every level, Adventurers gain a skill point to invest in their skill tree.
- Passive abilities are unlocked at levels 10/20/30/40 and each of the 3 main skill lines allow 5/5 points invested into each skill.
- Adventurers now have 100 Energy to activate skills, use it wisely!
- Other combat additions will be introduced in coming updates.

[b]Gameplay[/b]
- Crafting recipes have had their XP gain adjusted.
- The Dwarfia and Giantia NPC have released the Jester from his dialog duties.
- All dungeons should now have their own unique music tracks!
- Some previously existing music tracks were adjusted.
- The Imp is now reachable in the Druid Grove.
- Max Energy, Energy On Hit, and Energy Regen stats now roll on legendary items.
- Weapon Damage is now shown in the Character Sheet instead of Ranged/Melee to be more in line with tooltips and adding stats to Adventurers.
- Arcane and Holy Spellpower were combined into one stat: Spellpower. Based on the class, INT or WIS now grants Spellpower making it easier to know what stats to adjust (new skill tooltips) for Rangers, Clerics, Wizards and Paladins.
- Dual Wield is now in the game for Barbarians, Monks, Warriors and Rogues. This is an adjustable chance for the offhand weapon to make an attack on any skill use or normal attack.
- Filtering for equipment just got easier. Each Adventurer now saves filters and automatically filters equippable items.
- Inventory is now much easier to sort with smaller icons and roman numerals to indicate tier and a number at the bottom right to indicate iLVL.
- Selling in the shop is now easier with a new smart filter by rarity.
- MOUSE WHEEL!  Many windows are now scrollable with the mouse wheel... welcome to 1995! :)

[b]Art[/b]
- The Castle now has its own scene! From here you can use the Blacksmith, upgrade the Castle, and visit the Graveyard.
- The Graveyard now has its own scene as well! It functions the same as before and expect some fun epitaphs to enter sometime soon.
- The Town has received some animations, expect more improvements soon.

[b]Other[/b]
- An entirely new save and load system has been rolled into the game. This will make cloud saving, multiple saves, and Ironman mode possible in the near future!
- Lots of minor bug fixes and tweaks.

notes.title: AM Devlog #5
notes.content:
[i]Hello!

Welcome to another edition of AM Devlog! AM Devlogs are weekly updates on the development progress of Adventurer Manager. These Devlogs highlight our philosophy of the importance of transparency and player feedback.[/i]

Hooray! We've released our first major content patch of Early Access last week! This was a big milestone for us as the Blacksmith system was something we had been working on for quite a while. We were very pleased with the end-result and according to your feedback, you like it too! Now that we've gotten our first big content release out of the way we are going to do our hardest to bring regular updates to you at generally two week intervals. We may sometimes release early, sometimes later, but we will do our hardest for two week patch timelines. That being said, let's move on to what's in store for our next update!

Our last patch saw the introduction of a beautiful, new UI scene for towns. Naturally I'm sure you were wondering why the Castle doesn't have it's own. Well wonder no longer, because next patch will see a new Castle UI scene brought to us by our incredible artist [b]Amy Martins[/b]! Looking similar to the Town scene, the Castle will feature the Blacksmith, your Castle (where Castle Upgrades will be located), a Jeweler (not implemented yet), the Graveyard, and a brand new NPC who will be your Respec guide! With the new skill system coming soon he will allow you to respec your Adventurer's Skills and Attributes but for a hefty fee. In future updates the Castle in the background of the image will upgrade its appearance to reflect your upgrades. We're excited to continue to deliver regular art and UI updates alongside our major system developments.

[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog5/castle_area_preview.png[/img]
[i]Castle Scene Preview[/i]

Wait, that's not all! In addition to the Castle scene, there will be a brand new Graveyard scene created by our other amazing artist, [b]Alannah Linkhorn[/b]! This scene will replace the boring list of Tombstones and deliver a beautifully crafted scene that will endlessly populate with your dead Adventurers. Right now the gravestones will all be similar in appearance, but eventually the quality of the marker will reflect the level of the Adventurer. When you click a Tombstone that shows a name and Adventurer Level, a pop-up marker will appear that will list information about the Adventurer as well as how he died. There will be buttons you may use to loot the Adventurer, Resurrect him, or remove him from the game permanently. This should make the Graveyard far more interesting and certainly more visually appealing.

[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog5/graveyard_scene_preview.png[/img]
[i]Graveyard Scene Preview[/i]

While these features are awesome, I'm aware that most people are interested in the massive Skill changes we've been talking about. Here's a quick recap of what you can expect when these Skill changes hit in the next patch. First, there [b]WILL BE A WIPE[/b]. Unfortunately due to the massive changes required for the new skills, we will have to wipe all data. We assure you it will be worth it though. Skills will have investable Skill Points that are obtained every Adventurer Level. You may invest up to 5 points in each Skill. There are 4 different themed Lines of skills you may invest per Adventurer with 16 total skills with 12 actives and 4 passives. Each Skill will cost Energy and every Adventurer will start with 100 Energy at the beginning of every Encounter. The lower tier Skills will be weak but cost little Energy whereas the higher tier abilities will be massive but with massive Energy Costs. It will be up to you to strategically use your damage, buffs, and debuffs while maintaining your Energy levels. Early on you will not see much Energy regeneration but in later levels on higher quality gear there will be Energy on Hit, Energy Regen, and other methods to regain Energy in fights. Lastly, all 8 base Classes will be hireable when this patch hits.

We have been hard at work getting these Skills ready to push to you and they are almost there. The skills will come in a two part release with the first on being the base Skills with the Energy and the following release two weeks after will contain the special Class and Party abilities that utilize Power generated from hitting and being hit. While we are trying our hardest to balance the Skills we are aware that we may not get it right, so we really need your help in figuring out which Skills work and which don't. With our new system of creating and implementing Skills, editing and updating existing Skills is a quick hotfix for us whereas our old system was complex and tedious. We personally cannot wait to play these changes ourselves and hope you feel the same way.

________________________________________________________________

[b]AM Team Member Feature[/b]

AM Team Member Feature is a new segment in our weekly Devlogs. Every week or so I will feature one of our team members who is currently working on AM. Leading off the new segment is our [i]Assistant Designer and Special Effects Artist, [b]Michael Walker[/b][/i].

[img]http://va-studios.com/sites/all/themes/images/michael.jpg[/img]

[b]Who are you and what are your duties on Adventurer Manager?[/b]
 
My name is Michael Walker and I am the Special Effects Artist/Utility Guy on AM. I also work on the Class Skills. I fit into a bunch of different roles as I have a varied background. From 3D modeling and animation to special effects. I got my degree in Game Design and spend a lot of my time trying to learn every process of game development.
 
[b]What are you working on right now?[/b]
 
Currently I am working on the re-imagining of the Class skills system as well as the continued implementation of the special effects (visual and sound) for AM.
 
[b]What is a major feature that you have created or developed?[/b]
 
I, alongside Thomas, have helped created the class combat/skill systems. I am also in charge of the special effects systems, both visual and sound.
 
[b]What are your favorite aspects of working on Adventurer Manager and with VAStudios?[/b]
 
My favorite aspect of working on Adventurer Manager is working on a game that I find interesting. Also being able to work on a project with like-minded individuals has been a dream come true. 
 
[b]Do you have anything else you'd like to share with fans and those who may be interested in AM but have yet to purchase it?[/b]
 
I would let fans and those that are waiting to purchase the game know that if you are waiting on a better combat system with special effects, you shouldn’t have to wait too much longer. We are working as quickly as we can to deliver something that is both fun and visually pleasing.  

________________________________________________________________

That's all for this week's edition of AM Devlog! If you have any questions or comments about the game or these Devlogs, please leave a comment or post on our Steam Discussion boards or on our Studio forums at http://www.va-studios.com. Thanks so much for your continued support of Adventurer Manager. If you love the game, please tell a friend or twelve!

[i]Happy Adventuring![/i]
Thomas Spradling
Game Designer & Producer
VAStudios

notes.title: Build 0.4.26 - Blacksmith, Level Cap Increase, & New Adventurer Art!
notes.content:
It's been a couple of weeks since Early Access began but we're finally bringing you our first major content patch that introduces 4 new zones, 12 more levels, new art for Adventurers, and the Blacksmith!

[b]The Blacksmith![/b]
- The Blacksmith is now available from the Castle to craft equipment. Blacksmithing requires salvaged materials.
- Items may now be salvaged and turned into crafting materials.
- Gems have been seen dropping across various dungeons which can be used to guarantee stat rolls on crafted items. Reports indicate minibosses and bosses may be hoarding most of them....

[b]Game[/b]
- There is a new in game resolution changing option in the options menu.  This should allow you to change from windowed to full screen mode without having to exit the game (hurray).

[b]Gameplay[/b]
- Level Cap increased to 33.
- The story continues with 4 New Dungeons: the Mountain Pass, the Orc Camp, the Haunted Mansion, and the Farm.
- 2 New Races of Adventurers can be hired when unlocked, the Giant and the Dwarf.
- A big balance pass to Armor and HP was made.  The effect CON has on HP has been reduced, making it less vital of a requirement on every piece of gear.
- Major adjustments to how Constitution affects MaxHP were made and all classes have had their HP granted per level adjusted as well.
- Armor values were changed across the board resulting in more physical mitigation by all classes, notably plate wearers with shields.
- Treasure chests' chances of dropping higher quality items have been slightly increased.

[b]Art[/b]
- All Adventurers and their armor received brand new art!
- Female Adventurers now have their own character model!
- Over a dozen more male and female hairstyles and beards added.
- Updated male ghost and added female ghosts.
- Halflings have lost their shoes.
- Skin colors and eye colors have been changed slightly.
- Elves are now only lighter skin colors to prepare for their darker cousins....
- Elves have their own head art with ears!
- New portal art was introduced to match the updated Dungeon UI.

[b]UI[/b]
- Weapons that can be equipped in either hand are now listed as One-Handed in tooltips and Mainhand if only equippable in the main hand.
- The Town has received a facelift! There is a new UI for main towns (Castle and racial specific town Art to come soon).
- Secondary mini boss objectives are now displayed in the dungeon. Expect even more secondary objectives in the future.
- Dungeon UI re-designed. Updates to this will be ongoing.
- The minimap is now used for all dungeon movement making the dungeon map a reference only.
- A new resolution selector has been introduced in the Options menu from the world map.

[b]Bugs[/b]
- Fixed a bug allowing stats to be invested in the wrong characters.
- Fixed a bug causing combat to freeze if a monster dies to a damage over time effect at the start of their turn.
- Fixed a bug resulting in overflowing inventory eventually causing bugged items.
- Many other minor tweaks and fixes.

- The Blacksmith is now available from the Castle to craft equipment. Blacksmithing requires salvaged materials.
- Items may now be salvaged and turned into crafting materials.
- Gems have been seen dropping across various dungeons which can be used to guarantee stat rolls on crafted items. Reports indicate minibosses and bosses may be hoarding most of them....

[b]Game[/b]
- There is a new in game resolution changing option in the options menu.  This should allow you to change from windowed to full screen mode without having to exit the game (hurray).

[b]Gameplay[/b]
- Level Cap increased to 33.
- The story continues with 4 New Dungeons: the Mountain Pass, the Orc Camp, the Haunted Mansion, and the Farm.
- 2 New Races of Adventurers can be hired when unlocked, the Giant and the Dwarf.
- A big balance pass to Armor and HP was made.  The effect CON has on HP has been reduced, making it less vital of a requirement on every piece of gear.
- Major adjustments to how Constitution affects MaxHP were made and all classes have had their HP granted per level adjusted as well.
- Armor values were changed across the board resulting in more physical mitigation by all classes, notably plate wearers with shields.
- Treasure chests' chances of dropping higher quality items have been slightly increased.

[b]Art[/b]
- All Adventurers and their armor received brand new art!
- Female Adventurers now have their own character model!
- Over a dozen more male and female hairstyles and beards added.
- Updated male ghost and added female ghosts.
- Halflings have lost their shoes.
- Skin colors and eye colors have been changed slightly.
- Elves are now only lighter skin colors to prepare for their darker cousins....
- Elves have their own head art with ears!
- New portal art was introduced to match the updated Dungeon UI.

[b]UI[/b]
- Weapons that can be equipped in either hand are now listed as One-Handed in tooltips and Mainhand if only equippable in the main hand.
- The Town has received a facelift! There is a new UI for main towns (Castle and racial specific town Art to come soon).
- Secondary mini boss objectives are now displayed in the dungeon. Expect even more secondary objectives in the future.
- Dungeon UI re-designed. Updates to this will be ongoing.
- The minimap is now used for all dungeon movement making the dungeon map a reference only.
- A new resolution selector has been introduced in the Options menu from the world map.

[b]Bugs[/b]
- Fixed a bug allowing stats to be invested in the wrong characters.
- Fixed a bug causing combat to freeze if a monster dies to a damage over time effect at the start of their turn.
- Fixed a bug resulting in overflowing inventory eventually causing bugged items.
- Many other minor tweaks and fixes.

notes.title: AM Devlog #4 (Part 1)
notes.content:
[i]Hello![/i]

Welcome to another edition of AM Devlog! AM Devlogs are weekly updates on the development progress of Adventurer Manager. These Devlogs highlight our philosophy of the importance of transparency and player feedback.

Welcome to the two part 4th AM Devlog! This is a very exciting for Devlog for us because it will highlight two huge changes that are coming soon. This will be a text-heavy but I assure you it will be worth it! The first new feature is an overview of our skill changes. The second is an overview of a brand new, never announced upcoming management feature!

Our current skill system has served us well up until recently. It's long been something we wanted to improve and make more robust. Today we're ready to share with you what we've been designing and working on for changes to our skills. Every level an Adventurer will gain a skill point. You will be able to invest these points in up to 12 possible active skills and 4 possible passive skills with 5 of 5 investable skill points per skill. Unlike some other games in the past, we are not limiting the higher tier skills by points invested or even level. You will be able to attain the 'top' skill in one tree by level 4 in the new system. If you want, you can make a 'jack of all skills' Adventurer and put 1 point into all of your skills. This may not be the best option though, as the bonus for investing all 5 skillpoints into a specific skill will be worth it! Adventurer Manager is all about the Adventurers and in this new system with only 49 investable skill points over 16 skills with 5/5 investable points, you will only ever be able to maximize 10 of them. This new arrangement will allow for some interesting variations in Adventurers of the same class as a Warrior could specialize in damage dealing skills, party buffs and protects, or tanking and defense.

[img=https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog4/warrior_skilltree_preview.png]
[i]Early Warrior Skill Tree[/i]

Okay that's how the skill tree will work but what about how it's used in combat? Well, we've tossed out Cooldowns entirely! Now, every skill will cost Energy. Energy will be a flat 100 for all classes. Each skill, based on its tier, will cost a certain amount of Energy to use. The Energy pool will refresh between each encounter. The benefit to this system, as well as allowing access to almost all of our skills at lower level, allows for combat to be incredibly more tactical. Putting the skills you want in your hands to use anytime you want allows you to determine the best action to take in a variety of encounter situations. Need to drop the armor on that Zombie to hit him harder? Cast out a -Armor skill from your Warrior before you drop him down with your Rogue's high damage skills. An easy encounter of bats that will be a breeze? Just blow all your high Energy, high damage attacks to end the encounter quickly. But wait! That's not all!

In addition to expending Energy with attacks there will be another bar called Power that counts up! As you use abilities and take damage (choosing to Defend will generate more) you will gain Power in the respective Adventurer's Power bar. When you've reached a certain threshold you'll be able to use a special class ability! These are still in design at the moment but you'll be able to pick 1 permanent skill of a few options per class. When your Power bar has been filled you'll be able to unleash your Class's ultimate ability! In the case of a Cleric, your options will be a Resurrection, Full Group Heal, Instant Kill Undead or some others! We're not done there either!

Along with the individual Adventurer's Power bar, there will be a Party Power Bar! This bar will build up among all Adventurers and based on the Class arrangement of your party you will able to use a party ultimate ability. These will be slottable skills that unlock based on class arrangement in a party and you may choose the one you want before you enter a dungeon with a specific party. These will primarily be used in longer encounters like Boss fights to deal heavy damage or rescue your party in distress. We're incredibly excited to bring you these skill changes and we are certain it will be worth the wait!

With these changes, the last 3 classes in the base set of classes will be enabled for hire! These include the Barbarian, Paladin, and Monk. The Barbarian is a heavy damage melee combatant who can also pull his weight on the frontline as a dodge tank. The Paladin will be a hybrid between the Cleric and Warrior. Instead of focusing on Armor to tank, the Paladin will focus on blocking and some minor heals. The Monk is a little more interesting. He will focus on multi-hits with dual wield fists. With the Monk we are introducing a great change to dual wield, which is the chance on attack for the offhand weapon to make a separate attack. In essence, any class that dual wields weapons will have a flat chance to attack with the offhand weapon. The base amount will be most likely around 25% (it's still being decided), but it will be able to be raised with passives, abilities and other upcoming features. The Monk has abilities that cause dual hits with the offhand as well as other abilities and passives that raise his chance to dual wield hit. We've been wanting to bring these last few classes to you for a while and they are definitely coming soon!

[i](Continued in [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/280320/announcements/detail/1855792945830912902]Part 2[/url])[/i]

notes.title: AM Devlog #3
notes.content:
[i]Hello![/i]

Welcome to another edition of AM Devlog! AM Devlogs are weekly updates on the development progress of Adventurer Manager. These Devlogs highlight our philosophy of the importance of transparency and player feedback.

I'd like to start off this Devlog talking about the upcoming series of patches we are working on as well as their timetables for release. We had originally hoped to release a big content patch this week, but it looks it will be pushed to sometime later next week. We're bummed that you'll have to wait another week or so to see the changes, but it will definitely be worth it! Let me tell you why. 

One of the reasons we are waiting is because we have a new UI menu that will replace the boring one I showed you in the last Devlog. It is part of our committed efforts on UI redesign and we're really excited about giving you these neat, immersive scenes. The other reason it's being held back a week is because of the implementation of the Gems that will be used to create items with particular Attributes. We considered releasing it this week without the Gems but we felt that it was a huge component of Blacksmithing that needed to be included.

[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/blacksmith_preview2.png[/img]
[i]Early Blacksmith UI[/i]

The patch next week will include the Blacksmith and the increased level cap to 33 as well as 2 new Towns, 2 new Races, and 4 new dungeons! The 2 new Towns will be Giantia and Dwarfia and the Giant and Dwarf race will be hireable when they are unlocked through the Story. The 4 new dungeons are the Mountain Pass (featured in our Steam Trading Cards) full of snow bandits, the Orc Camp (full of orcs, duh), the Haunted Mansion (full of evil and ghostly things), and the Farm (full of some...interesting farm animals). We are really excited to get these new areas out to you with a 12 level increase to the cap! 

[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/mountain_pass_preview.png[/img]
[i]Mountain Pass[/i]

[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/snowbanditranger_preview.png[/img]
[i]Snow Bandit[/i]

With these updates, it is with heavy regret to inform you that the remaining classes will not make it to the patch next week. We had originally wanted to bring you all 3 of the remaining classes, Barbarian, Paladin, Monk with this update but due to some massive, massive skill overhauls, these will have to wait a couple more weeks.

Don't fret too much though because this week's Devlog features a big surprise that should make it into next week's patch! I'll let the screenshots do the explaining:

[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/newmod1.png[/img][img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/oldmodel1.png[/img]
[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/newmod2.png[/img][img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/oldmodel2.png[/img]
[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/newmod3.png[/img][img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/oldmodel3.png[/img]
[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/newmod4.png[/img][img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/oldmodel4.png[/img]
[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/newmod5.png[/img][img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/oldmodel5.png[/img]
[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/newmod6.png[/img][img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/oldmodel6.png[/img]
[i]Adventurer Comparison New/Old[/i]

That's right, new Adventurer sprites! Our quirky original Adventurers will be replaced with brand new, larger and more detailed sprites. These new sprites allow us to have much more room on the Adventurers to craft amazing looking equipment. It also lets us have enough space to provide visual indications of gender! We're always improving the look of AM as we develop and we're happy to provide you with a major visual improvement. In time we are going to consider more complex animations for them as well, but for now, I hope you enjoy the new look!

That's about all for next week's patch, but I'm going to take a bit to talk about some other development that's going on. First up, the Dungeon UI overhaul! I showed off a small sketch of this last week but I wanted to provide you all with an neat update on it. It will now feature a neat Courier character who is in charge of making sure you receive your royal notifications! He will sit idle in the Dungeon UI but when something needs your attention, he will wave at you. Clicking him will unfurl a large Scroll that will give you indications of the goings on in your kingdom. 

[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/courier_preview.png[/img][img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog3/dungeon_scroll_preview.png[/img]
[i]Courier & Scroll Menu[/i]

Eventually AutoQuests will be able to be Auto-Completed from this menu, Resting Adventurers will indicate when they have rested, and other upcoming management features will have indicators. This menu will allow you to continue to move your favored party through their dungeon in manual mode while being able to manage your kingdom easily and efficiently. As part of this new UI, you will be able to 'pause' the dungeon you are currently in to go back to the world map and take actions. When you return to the party, you will be exactly where you left off. No more having to portal back to town to manage your Adventurers. Hooray!

That's about it for this edition of AM Devlog. Stay tuned for next week's where I will discuss a truly exciting feature that is coming down the pipe!

[i]Happy Adventuring![/i]
Thomas Spradling
Game Designer & Producer
VAStudios

We have hopefully resolved all our OSX issues and anyone who has purchased Early Access on Mac should now be seeing content streamed.  If you do not please let us know asap so we can investigate.

Now that we all full steam ahead and our programmer's (me) is starting to be able to type again, hopefully we will be releasing some good content next week.

Here are the patch notes for 0.4.17:
Gameplay
- Risk indicators should be more reliable when entering dungeons.
- Newly found or crafted items are now marked with a star in the inventory until the inventory window is closed. This allows players to view the inventory and see any items they have not seen before while in the Character Sheet equip window.
- Other party members and parties are now selectable in the Character Sheet for better gear management.
- Parties are available for use much earlier in the game and reserve slots have been adjusted to +2 per party.  Ex. First party unlock = 6 total adventurers, 2nd party unlock = 12 total adventurers, 3rd = 18, 4th = 24.

Bugs
- The Crazed Squatter has thrown down his staff and properly found a scepter to do proper damage with.
- Fixed a bug resulting in Minibosses not dropping proper loot.
- Fixed Thin Blade not displaying correctly.
- Fixed a bug with Warrior's Bash enhancement not stunning for proper rounds.
- Fixed a bug causing failed Adventures to not despawn the encounter of monsters.

notes.title: Review: Adventurer Manager is a must-have silly RPG
notes.content:
Shoost.co has a look at Adventurer Manager! See the full article over at http://shoost.co/2014/05/05/adventurer-manager-is-a-must-have-silly-rpg/

[b]Here's a few snippets from the article:[/b]

[i]
"Here’s Adventurer Manager’s breakdown: You are a king and need to save your kingdom, Adventuria, from the evil illusionist named Miraj. You need to hire adventurers and send them on epic quests to gather loot, save towns, rescue people, save waffles, murder 194 ladies, and entertain 157 lamps.

“Wait a minute, Val. You’re not making any sense! Entertain 157 lamps? Save waffles? Are you serious?”

Why yes, yes I am. You can even get experience and gold by going on a quest to comb some rocks. Is this the perfect game for the cynical populace of earth? Perhaps. Most likely. Okay, yes it is."

...

"Since the game is still in development, the community can help with reporting bugs and engaging in other discussions with the devs. There are also a whole bunch of planned features such as crafting, more management options, achievements, racial allegiance benefits, and more tutorials. With a lot on its plate, Vigilant Addiction Studios still has a ways to go to bring this game to its full potential, but it looks like they are on the right track."

[/i]

Article Credit: VALERIE ANNE CHIANG

notes.title: AM Devlog #2
notes.content:
[i]Hello![/i]

Welcome to another edition of AM Devlog! AM Devlogs are a weekly update about Adventurer Manager's development process to maintain our philosophy of transparency and the importance of player feedback.

As stated earlier in the week, our lead programmer had wrist surgery shortly after the EA release and is on the road to recovery. That being said, because he's awesome and is now probably part robot, he's still managed to update the game twice with small updates for our most requested changes. These were small changes like speeding up the walk time in dungeons as well as removing level-scaling, but they were definitely important and it's all because of you, the player's, vital feedback! Now on to the good stuff of what's coming down the pipe!

Adventurer Manager is very item centric and because we have a ton of items (seriously we have over 15 different weapon types), there are often holes in equipment as your party levels. To counteract those gaps we are implementing the Blacksmith in our next big update! Here's how it will work. Every item of a rarity up to legendary can be salvaged for a similar rarity resource that can be used to craft randomized items of that rarity. So for instance, if you salvage a few uncommons you'll be able to make a new uncommon, but not anything higher. Basically you'll need to salvage legendaries to make legendaries! You will be able to make all item types and the blacksmith will need to be leveled up to increase the tier of the gear being made. Okay so that's how completely randomized items are crafted, but how do I get the stats I want on crafted gear? Gems! Gems will have a chance of dropping off every encounter and they will be of a specific Attribute (str, dex, con, etc.) When you go to craft an item with your salvaged rarity resources you can use a gem to signify that as definitive Attribute to roll on that item. The rest of the modifiers on that item will be randomized. When it goes live you will be able to set 2 Attributes as a maximum with 2 Gems, and again the rest of the stats will be randomized. There will be multiple rarities of gems that increase the Attributes base value when it is rolled. We are really excited about this addition as it's been sitting at about 75% completeness for a few months just waiting for the right time to go in!

[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog2/blacksmith_preview.png[/img]
[i]Early Blacksmith Preview[/i]

Also one of our Artists, Amy Martins, has just completed the new town square UI! It looks amazing and I hope you think so too! This is just one of the many ongoing UI changes that are underway to replace many of the dull menus with beautifully crafted ones that really fit the style of AM.

[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog2/town_square_preview.png[/i]
[i]Town Square Preview[/i]

Speaking of UI changes, here's another upcoming one! Artist Alannah Linkhorn has designed this updated dungeon UI element and it's hot off the press as it just arrived in my inbox this morning! It's still being worked on, but we're liking where it's going!

[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog2/DungeonUICombatSketch_preview.jpg[/img]
[i]Improved Dungeon UI Preview[/i]

One of the other things you're going to see soon is the unlocking of the other parties much, much earlier in the game. By around level 10 you will have all 4 parties unlocked! With this we are also going to unlock all of the base 8 classes alongside the party unlocks! Oh wait, did I just say 8? Yes! The Barbarian, Paladin, and Monk are going to enter the game very, very soon. We are finalizing their skills and skill icon art. With the unlocking of the parties earlier and with all of the classes and their unique skill trees, we're really excited about all the unique combinations that will be used!

Finally, probably the biggest update we have coming your way is the extension of the level cap from 21 to 33! This extension will feature more story, 4 brand new dungeons with new monsters, minibosses, and bosses for each of them! These dungeons also feature more monsters than any others thus far! This level increase is also going to unlock 2 new races, the Giants and the Dwarves! Below is a preview of one of the new areas, the Orc Camp!

[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog2/orc_camp_preview.png[/img]
[i]The Orc Camp[/i]
[img]https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog2/orc_warrior_preview.png[/img]
[i]Orc Warrior[/i]


Well that's all for this week's edition of the AM Devlog. Stay tuned next week for more updates!

[i]Happy Adventuring![/i]
Thomas Spradling
Game Designer & Producer
VAStudios

Another small update to address some XP bugs and major pain points.

- Monsters now spawn random levels to add a bit more variety to dungeons. This addresses the issue of players finding it unbalanced to have monsters spawn in at their level without a chance to get any loot to offset.

- Added more monster animations.
- Adjusted the levels monsters start equipping items in early levels.
- Adjusted bonus HP Warrior's and Cleric's get per level. (Monsters also)
- Crypt - Less Adventurers are venturing into the Crypt resulting in the Zombie population to be slightly reduced.

​Bugs 
- Unique items no longer accidentally roll Enhanced Damage on armor sometimes.
- Fixed a bug causing item compare tooltips to incorrectly compare to the wrong item.
- Fixed a bug causing chest based item drops to incorrectly roll lower levels than intended.

- Fixed a major bug with XP rewards on quest turn in and encounters.

notes.title: AM Devlog #1
notes.content:
[b]Adventurer Manager Devlog #1[/b]

[i]Hello![/i] Welcome to the first Adventurer Manager (AM) Devlog! These devlogs will be a part of our ongoing mission to keep you up to date with the behind the scenes development of the game as well as remain as transparent as possible in the development plans for Adventurer Manager.

Early Access is finally almost here! We’re incredibly thrilled about where the game is at the moment but we have a long road ahead full of exciting updates. The game has come such a long way from when we first started working on it and we can’t wait to continue to improve it with you. Looking through our art today, I came across this old image that was used as part of the pitch image for AM. I’ve included a current image for reference. Kind of crazy huh? I certainly think so! We have an amazing team and we’re going to work our asses off to make sure we can deliver a game you’re as excited about playing as we are about making it.

[img=https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog1/early_adventurer_manager.jpg]
[i]Early Image for Adventurer Manager (Cave Dungeon)[/i]

[img=https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog1/Cave%201.png]
[i]Current Image of Adventurer Manager (Cave Dungeon)[/i]

Now that we’re here at Early Access you will get to see some of the cool ideas as they come to fruition week to week. What’s even more awesome and more exciting for us is allowing you, the players to have significant input on the systems and features in AM! We will be reading up on the discussions on Steam daily and don’t hesitate to drop us a line on our forums at va-studios.com.


[i]All[/i] that being said, now it’s time to get into the nitty gritty of what we’ve been working on right now! There has always been a long debate among the team about whether onscreen UI for the Dungeons should be minimal or robust and informational. Up until this point, the game has contained very minimal on-screen UI in dungeons. While this is nice for the aesthetics of the dungeons it is not very informative. We've decided at this point to move forward with an on-screen UI for dungeons. Here’s an early sample that you will see in Early Access:

[img=https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog1/in_dungeon_bottom_ui.png]

The benefits of this change are two-fold. The first one, the most obvious one that was just mentioned was the ability to provide far more information about what’s happening in the dungeon, both in combat as well as in ease of moving from room to room with our new minimap compass feature. The second benefit of this change is that it lets us shrink down our dungeon art to basically appear more crisp on the screen while still retaining our retro look. Previously, the size in pixels between the other screens and the dungeons was pretty substantial, so much so that in my opinion the dungeons were kind of hard on the eyes.

The minimap compass will let you quickly travel the different directions on the map without having to open the full map. Arrows will appear for possible directions that will pulse. In directions you cannot travel, the arrows will disappear. This should make navigating the dungeons much easier. We’re really excited about this change and are hard at work making sure it is filled with useful information as well as working on improving the look of the UI piece.

Another thing that went in recently was ghosts! Previously, when an adventurer died he was replaced with a permanent floating tombstone that would awkwardly glide around with the party in the faint hope that the adventurer would be rezzed before the party returned to town. Now a fun ghost will appear and float alongside the party until they are rezzed or return to town where the adventurer is then deposited in the graveyard.
[img=https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog1/human_ghost.png]

We’re also working on a really awesome new scene that will become our Town UI. Right now when you click a town you just get three big and boring buttons. The new UI will be a scene of that town with different buildings and NPC’s working in the scene. Long term we plan to have one themed for each Race, but for the short term when this goes in, it will replace all of the town menus everywhere. This should hit fairly soon! I’ve included a WIP image below:

[img=https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog1/town_sample.jpg]

These things listed above are all fantastic, but largely aesthetic. I’d like to take a minute to talk about a planned system that’s going in! We’re calling it our Injuries system. When your party is on an Adventure in a Dungeon and one of your adventurer’s health drops below a certain amount of HP he will receive an Injury and Injuries will be cumulative! The Injury will be located in one of 4 possible body locations, each with their own negative effects: Head, Body, Arms, and Legs. Just as an example: Head Injuries cause the adventurer to receive a -%ToHit value whereas Body Injuries will cause the adventurer to lose -%Max HP. One or two Injuries will be not terribly detrimental, but if you let them accumulate, the effects will definitely be noticeable. How do you heal those Injuries though?! Injuries will be healed in a brand new Town service, the Inn! The Inn will provide multiple quality bed options for resting adventurers that have tiered costs as well as tiered rest times. There will always be a free sleep option, but the time it takes to heal 1 Injury will be pretty severe. The higher quality beds will heal Injuries much faster. In addition, future upgrades will reduce these costs and reduce the time if that is the upgrade you decide to invest in. Adventurer Manager is about the Adventurers and this system helps us get closer to our goal of having you, the player, use more than 4-8 Adventurers at all times and have a large pool of Reserves that you are utilizing. Having your beefy Warrior out of the action for a while will hopefully make Adventuring more challenging and exciting!

One last thing I want to mention that we are working on: Side Adventures! Right now the Dungeons are a bit grindy as you work your way towards the boss to complete the story and advance. We really want to give you more reasons to stay and explore in the Dungeons. Coming soon we will have Side Adventures for each location. These will be simple tasks to complete in each dungeon and some will most likely require a Dungeon Reset or two to complete the tasks. They will reward you with XP and Gold and possibly items for completion and they will complete immediately without having to go turn them in. They will also be repeatable! Side Adventures will generally consist of Killing a number of X Monster, Collecting a number of X items, Defeating specific mini-bosses, etc. This will also allow us to bring in our silly randomized dialog that we use in our Auto Adventures.

That’s it for the first Devlog of Adventurer Manager, I hope you’ll continue to follow along with me as the development for AM progresses! If there is anything you’d like me to talk about during these Devlogs, don’t hesitate to post in our Steam Discussions our on our VAStudios forums!

[i]Happy Adventuring![/i]
Thomas Spradling (froren)
Game Designer & Producer
VAStudios

[img=https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog1/Cave%201.png]
[i]Current Image of Adventurer Manager (Cave Dungeon)[/i]

Now that we’re here at Early Access you will get to see some of the cool ideas as they come to fruition week to week. What’s even more awesome and more exciting for us is allowing you, the players to have significant input on the systems and features in AM! We will be reading up on the discussions on Steam daily and don’t hesitate to drop us a line on our forums at va-studios.com.


[i]All[/i] that being said, now it’s time to get into the nitty gritty of what we’ve been working on right now! There has always been a long debate among the team about whether onscreen UI for the Dungeons should be minimal or robust and informational. Up until this point, the game has contained very minimal on-screen UI in dungeons. While this is nice for the aesthetics of the dungeons it is not very informative. We've decided at this point to move forward with an on-screen UI for dungeons. Here’s an early sample that you will see in Early Access:

[img=https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog1/in_dungeon_bottom_ui.png]

The benefits of this change are two-fold. The first one, the most obvious one that was just mentioned was the ability to provide far more information about what’s happening in the dungeon, both in combat as well as in ease of moving from room to room with our new minimap compass feature. The second benefit of this change is that it lets us shrink down our dungeon art to basically appear more crisp on the screen while still retaining our retro look. Previously, the size in pixels between the other screens and the dungeons was pretty substantial, so much so that in my opinion the dungeons were kind of hard on the eyes.

The minimap compass will let you quickly travel the different directions on the map without having to open the full map. Arrows will appear for possible directions that will pulse. In directions you cannot travel, the arrows will disappear. This should make navigating the dungeons much easier. We’re really excited about this change and are hard at work making sure it is filled with useful information as well as working on improving the look of the UI piece.

Another thing that went in recently was ghosts! Previously, when an adventurer died he was replaced with a permanent floating tombstone that would awkwardly glide around with the party in the faint hope that the adventurer would be rezzed before the party returned to town. Now a fun ghost will appear and float alongside the party until they are rezzed or return to town where the adventurer is then deposited in the graveyard.
[img=https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog1/human_ghost.png]

We’re also working on a really awesome new scene that will become our Town UI. Right now when you click a town you just get three big and boring buttons. The new UI will be a scene of that town with different buildings and NPC’s working in the scene. Long term we plan to have one themed for each Race, but for the short term when this goes in, it will replace all of the town menus everywhere. This should hit fairly soon! I’ve included a WIP image below:

[img=https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/1950450/AM_Devlogs/Devlog1/town_sample.jpg]

These things listed above are all fantastic, but largely aesthetic. I’d like to take a minute to talk about a planned system that’s going in! We’re calling it our Injuries system. When your party is on an Adventure in a Dungeon and one of your adventurer’s health drops below a certain amount of HP he will receive an Injury and Injuries will be cumulative! The Injury will be located in one of 4 possible body locations, each with their own negative effects: Head, Body, Arms, and Legs. Just as an example: Head Injuries cause the adventurer to receive a -%ToHit value whereas Body Injuries will cause the adventurer to lose -%Max HP. One or two Injuries will be not terribly detrimental, but if you let them accumulate, the effects will definitely be noticeable. How do you heal those Injuries though?! Injuries will be healed in a brand new Town service, the Inn! The Inn will provide multiple quality bed options for resting adventurers that have tiered costs as well as tiered rest times. There will always be a free sleep option, but the time it takes to heal 1 Injury will be pretty severe. The higher quality beds will heal Injuries much faster. In addition, future upgrades will reduce these costs and reduce the time if that is the upgrade you decide to invest in. Adventurer Manager is about the Adventurers and this system helps us get closer to our goal of having you, the player, use more than 4-8 Adventurers at all times and have a large pool of Reserves that you are utilizing. Having your beefy Warrior out of the action for a while will hopefully make Adventuring more challenging and exciting!

One last thing I want to mention that we are working on: Side Adventures! Right now the Dungeons are a bit grindy as you work your way towards the boss to complete the story and advance. We really want to give you more reasons to stay and explore in the Dungeons. Coming soon we will have Side Adventures for each location. These will be simple tasks to complete in each dungeon and some will most likely require a Dungeon Reset or two to complete the tasks. They will reward you with XP and Gold and possibly items for completion and they will complete immediately without having to go turn them in. They will also be repeatable! Side Adventures will generally consist of Killing a number of X Monster, Collecting a number of X items, Defeating specific mini-bosses, etc. This will also allow us to bring in our silly randomized dialog that we use in our Auto Adventures.

That’s it for the first Devlog of Adventurer Manager, I hope you’ll continue to follow along with me as the development for AM progresses! If there is anything you’d like me to talk about during these Devlogs, don’t hesitate to post in our Steam Discussions our on our VAStudios forums!

[i]Happy Adventuring![/i]
Thomas Spradling (froren)
Game Designer & Producer
VAStudios
